findings.observation: The source prints π(500y²−10y³)|_0^1=40π. The antiderivative of100y is50y², not500y².
findings.resolution: Replace500 by50. The final40π numerator and80°C weighted average then agree.
findings.derivation: d(50y²−10y³)/dy=100y−30y²; the printed500 would yield490π at1 rather than40π.

findings.observation: The lower radius appears as2r_i, while the board radius and all calculations use r_1.
findings.resolution: Read the annular sector as2r_1<r<3r_1, in agreement with the diagram and surrounding text.
findings.derivation: There is only one board radius parameter in this example; no sequence indexed by i is introduced.

findings.observation: The derivation assumes equally spaced samples, b>a and an integrable function. Weighted means require a nonzero finite total nonnegative weight.
findings.resolution: Use average_f=(1/(b−a))∫f for uniform x, and∫fw/∫w for the chosen nonnegative weightw with0<∫w<∞ and finite∫|f|w.
findings.derivation: Equal horizontal spacing produces the source Riemann sum; nonuniform equal-count samples would represent a different measure. For the unit semicircle ds=dθ, so uniform arclength uses(1/π)∫_0^πsinθdθ=2/π, different fromπ/4.

findings.observation: The distinction between volume and height averages is valid; only the500 typo is erroneous.
findings.resolution: Volume-weighted mean height is2/3m, while uniform-height mean is1/2m.
findings.derivation: With normalized volume weight2y on[0,1], E[y]=∫2y²dy=2/3; hence E[T]=100−30(2/3)=80. Uniform-height average gives100−30/2=85. Both lie between70 and100, and the cooler-volume explanation is consistent.

findings.location: Dart ce^(−r²), ring weighting and part/whole
findings.observation: The ratio assumes an isotropic planar Gaussian density on the whole plane, c>0, and the given annular-sector approximation of the target. ce^(−r²) by itself is not the one-dimensional radial probability density.
findings.resolution: Interpret it as areal density; the radial factor after normalization is pR(r)=2re^(−r²) forr≥0, and angle is uniform. For probabilities, part/whole means integrals of this weight.
findings.derivation: Whole-plane mass is2πc∫_0^∞re^(−r²)dr=πc, so normalized areal density isπ^−1e^(−r²). The angular interval is2/12=1/6 of a turn. A physical radius must be scaled: e^(−λr²), λ>0 with inverse-square-length units; the50% calibration suppliesλr1²=ln2.

findings.observation: The final about1% probability per dart is correct for the specified model; the source neglects(1/2)^9.
findings.derivation: The antiderivative yieldsP=(e^(−4r1²)−e^(−9r1²))/6. Board hit probability1−e^(−r1²)=1/2 gives the powers. Neglecting1/512 gives1/96≈1.0417%, still about1%. These are unconditional per-throw probabilities; conditioned on missing the board, divide by1/2, giving31/1536≈2.0182%. The source final sentence explicitly uses per dart.

findings.location: Gaussian solid computed by two unbounded slicing methods
findings.observation: The source calculates the shell limit correctly but passes between unbounded solid slices and Q² without explicitly proving convergence or justifying the passage. The result is correct.
findings.resolution: A bounded-domain squeeze supplies a direct justification without assuming Q is finite first.
findings.derivation: Let QR=∫_-R^R e^(−x²)dx. Over the square[−R,R]² the finite product integral equals QR². The disk of radiusR lies inside that square, which lies inside the disk of radius sqrt2 R. Nonnegative integrand givesπ(1−e^(−R²))≤QR²≤π(1−e^(−2R²)). Both bounds tendπ, so QR→sqrtπ. Positivity/evenness then establish the ordinary whole-line improper integral and both tail limits. This is reviewer-derived supplementation, not a proof displayed in the packet.

findings.observation: Q²=π alone has two algebraic roots; positivity of the integral selects the positive root. Sigma>0 is explicitly stated.
findings.resolution: Use t=x/(sqrt2 σ), dx=sqrt2 σdt, withσ>0; the density is[σsqrt(2π)]^−1 exp(−x²/(2σ²)).
findings.derivation: The enlarged original-source render confirmsσ is outside the radical in the denominator; this normalization is correct, not a source typo. Substitution gives integral1 directly fromQ=sqrtπ.

findings.observation: The source asserts the statistical meaning ofσ without computing moments.
findings.resolution: For this centered normal density, symmetry gives mean0 and the second moment isσ².
findings.derivation: Forσ=1, integrate x²e^(−x²/2): integration by parts gives integral x²e^(−x²/2)dx=integral e^(−x²/2)dx over the whole line since x e^(−x²/2)→0 at both ends. Normalization gives variance1. Scalingx=σt gives varianceσ²; positiveσ is the standard deviation. This is an independent supplement.

findings.observation: The picture shows a decreasing positive profile with no axes values. It cannot be the radial density2re^(−r²), which starts at0 and initially increases.
findings.resolution: Treat it as a schematic right half of a Gaussian areal/profile function, not as a plot of the radial integrand in the adjacent denominator.
findings.derivation: Derivative of2re^(−r²) is2e^(−r²)(1−2r²), so its peak is atr=1/sqrt2. The actual ring integration in the text includes the requiredr factor and remains correct.
